messages.author: 4b06c0bae2d1991d
messages.subject: mirtCAT with nuisance factors
parts:
I am trying to simulate a multidimensional CAT with a bifactor model. There is 1 general factor and 4 nuisance factors. Is there an optimal item selection rule for models with nuisance factors? I've found a citation for different types of Kullback-Leibler item selection that include a type for nuisance factors (https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-85461-8_4) but it is unclear to me if the modifications proposed to the KL criterion is available with KL or KLn item selection methods. Is there an optimal item selection method already programmed in mirtCAT that does a better job at only emphasizing the theoretically-meaningful factor, as opposed to all factors, including nuisance ones?

Thanks,
Aaron

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: mirtCAT with nuisance factors
parts:
Hi Aaron,

Sure, just supply a weights vector (design list input) where all the weight is placed on the general trait of interest. 

design <- list(weights <- c(1,0,0,0))

That will weight the fisher information matrices, pulling out only the terms that best load on the current general factor. I think I discuss this a bit in the JSS article. 

Phil
